concepts.label: endpoint-six singleton model
concepts.note: The auxiliary predicate holding exactly at n=6.

concepts.label: double-or-recycle transition shape
concepts.note: The formal disjunction shared with the actual exact-row transition but instantiated by a different predicate.

concepts.label: cofinality inference barrier

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: boundedDoubleOrRecycleModel n holds exactly when n=6. It is a free-standing one-point model, not the predicate of actual exact local Mersenne half rows.
statement_nodes.engine: exact definition of the auxiliary predicate
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: An explicit corpus-internal logical countermodel; no external novelty or priority claim is made.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The auxiliary predicate is not ExactLocalMersenneHalfRow and asserts nothing about the actual seam.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For n≥6, if the singleton model P holds at n, then P(2n-1) or there exists c with 4≤c≤n and P(2c-2). Since P(n) forces n=6, the proof takes the recycle branch c=4 and returns to endpoint 6.
statement_nodes.engine: unfolding the singleton predicate and using the fixed recycle witness c=4
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: An explicit corpus-internal logical countermodel; no external novelty or priority claim is made.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The theorem concerns only the auxiliary singleton predicate. It neither reformulates nor refutes the actual exact-row transition theorem.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The endpoint-six singleton model is not cofinal: it is false that for every N there exists n≥N with P(n). The witness threshold N=7 contradicts P(n) iff n=6.
statement_nodes.engine: the bounded singleton support and the threshold N=7
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: An explicit corpus-internal logical countermodel; no external novelty or priority claim is made.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: Noncofinality of this auxiliary predicate does not prove actual exact rows noncofinal. It refutes only inference from the abstract seeded transition shape alone and leaves strict-progress or independent arithmetic cofinality inputs available.

intra_zone_relations.basis: Unfolding the singleton definition reduces the transition to the fixed recycle witness c=4.
The predicate's support is the bounded singleton {6}.
A seeded predicate can obey this transition forever while remaining bounded, so the transition shape alone does not force endpoint growth.
